Website design Texarkana owners can rely on starts with a simple fact about the town: a big share of the people who spend money here do not live here. They drive in from small towns in Texas, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Louisiana for a doctor's appointment, a day of shopping or a part they cannot get at home, and most of them check a business online before they get in the car. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan building sites by hand from Big Sandy. You see a free demo first and pay one printed price.

Texarkana is two cities sharing one name, with State Line Avenue running down the border and a post office and federal courthouse that sits in both states at once. This page is about the Texas side, a city of about 36,000 people in recent Census Bureau counts.

Web design in Texarkana for a regional medical center

A 2025 overview from TexAmericas Center calls Texarkana the medical hub of a large rural healthcare market. CHRISTUS St. Michael has long been the biggest name, and in November 2024 CHRISTUS Health finished buying Wadley Regional Medical Center out of the Steward Health Care bankruptcy, keeping nearly all of its clinicians and staff.

Hospitals pull in a whole ring of smaller businesses: specialty clinics, physical therapists, home health agencies, pharmacies, medical supply stores, and the restaurants and hotels where families wait. A patient from two counties away searching for a clinic needs the street address, the right entrance, parking and hours on the first screen. If the site buries those, the phone rings with questions instead of appointments.

Three Texarkana businesses and what each page has to carry

The clinic down the street from the hospital

Insurance accepted, a map to the door, what to bring to a first visit, and a phone line answered when the front desk is busy.

The shop near Richmond Road

Richmond Road near Interstate 30 is the main shopping strip, with newer growth to the west toward the University Avenue interchange. A small shop there needs hours and a reason to stop that a big box cannot give.

The trade that covers the whole area

A plumber, roofer or electrician working Bowie County and beyond should list the towns served, the licenses held and an easy way to ask for a quote.

Paychecks from the depot and a growing campus

Red River Army Depot, in Bowie County, began in World War II when more than 20,000 construction workers turned 18,000 acres into an ordnance depot, and it still ranks among the area's major employers, along with CHRISTUS St. Michael, Cooper Tire and Texas A&M University-Texarkana. Depot workers and contractors are local customers for every kind of service.

The university is the fast mover. Texas A&M-Texarkana reported fall 2025 enrollment about 40% higher than in fall 2023, then a seventh straight record term in spring 2026, and in fall 2026 a ninth straight record with about 30% more students than the year before. Students and new staff search for haircuts, apartments, food and car repair the same way: on a phone, by what is closest. Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence, so a page that names what you do and where you are gives you a fair shot at those searches.

Built in East Texas, delivered to Texarkana

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Texarkana. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

You approve each page before launch. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.

Where Texarkana owners can get free business help

Northeast Texas SBDC, Texarkana office

Free counseling for small businesses. The Ark-Tex Council of Governments lists Bowie County, which includes Texarkana, Texas, in the Northeast Texas SBDC's service area, and the center keeps a Texarkana office.

Texarkana USA Regional Chamber of Commerce

A membership association that brings together businesses on both sides of the state line, a natural place to meet other owners and hear about local programs.

We are not affiliated with either one. Both are good first calls for a new or growing business.

Common questions

Who does website design in Texarkana?

Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites for Texarkana businesses remotely from Big Sandy, Texas. Maurice Johnson writes and builds every page himself, and you see a free demo of your own site before anyone asks for money. There is no office in Texarkana.

How much does web design in Texarkana cost?

With us, the price is printed and paid once: $497 for the five-page Starter, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. Other designers price by quote, so compare what each one includes, who owns the finished site and what you pay every month after launch.

My business is on the Arkansas side. Can you still build my site?

Yes. We build for businesses anywhere, and the free demo works the same way. The local facts on this page are about the Texas side, Bowie County and the trade area around it; we would write your pages around your own address and customers.

Do medical and dental offices in Texarkana need a different kind of website?

They need clearer basics. Patients driving in from small towns want the exact address, parking and entrance, hours, which insurance you take and a phone number that dials with one tap. We write those pages plainly. We do not build patient portals or records systems; those come from your practice software vendor.

Can I sell products online through the site?

Online stores are not part of our packages, and we would rather say so now. A Texarkana shop can still show what it carries, its hours and how to call ahead to hold an item, which is often what a customer an hour away really wants before the drive.

Want to see your Texarkana website before you spend a dollar?

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
